title: Some Applications of Trigonometry: Heights and Distances

standard_text: Heights and distances: angle of elevation, angle of depression; simple problems on heights and distances; problems should not involve more than two right triangles; angles of elevation / depression should be only 30°, 45° and 60° (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Heights and Distances worksheet (NCERT Chapter 9): angles of elevation and depression, towers, lighthouses, kites, ladders and two-triangle problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Angles of elevation and depression use 30°, 45° and 60°.
body_html:
How it works

The angle of elevation is the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when you look up. The angle of depression is the angle when you look down.

Draw the right triangle, mark the angle, then use tan θ = height/distance (or sin, cos when a slanting length is involved).

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. The angle of depression from A to B equals the angle of elevation from B to A.

Example

A tower is 30 m from a point where the angle of elevation is 60°. Find its height.

tan 60° = h/30

h = 30√3

Answer: 30√3 m ≈ 51.9 m

Example

From the top of a 75 m lighthouse, the angle of depression of a ship is 45°. How far is the ship?

tan 45° = 75/d

Answer: 75 m

Common mistakes

  • Writing h = d/tan θ when the distance is known. It is h = d × tan θ.
  • Marking the angle of depression at the bottom of the figure. It is at the observer's eye, below the horizontal.
  • Using tan 30° = √3. tan 30° = 1/√3 and tan 60° = √3.

faq.q: What is an angle of elevation?
faq.a: The angle between the horizontal line and the line of sight to an object above the observer's eye.

faq.q: What is an angle of depression?
faq.a: The angle between the horizontal line and the line of sight to an object below the observer's eye. It equals the angle of elevation seen from the object.

faq.q: Which ratio is used in heights and distances?
faq.a: Usually tan θ = height/horizontal distance. Use sin or cos when a slanting length such as a ladder or kite string is given.

faq.q: Why is the answer often left as 20√3 m?
faq.a: Exact answers keep the surd. If asked, use √3 ≈ 1.73 to get a decimal, for example 20√3 ≈ 34.6 m.

items.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground is 30°. After walking 25 m towards the tower, the angle becomes 60°. Find the height of the tower.
items.e: Let the height be h and the second distance y: h = y√3 and h = (y + 25)/√3. So 3y = y + 25, y = 252 m and h = 25√3/2 m.

items.q: Two poles of equal height stand on either side of a road 60 m wide. From a point on the road between them, the angles of elevation of their tops are 60° and 30°. Find the height of each pole.
items.e: Distances x and 60 − x: h = x√3 and h = (60 − x)/√3. So 3x = 60 − x, x = 15 m and h = 15√3 m.
